page.layout: One page of running text, one column, full width. Running head at top. Below the text a single line of catchword-like ornament, no further blocks. Margin notes: none legible beyond a small mark at the right edge of the text (a reference sign near "ris" and the dot at the right of "corpo-").

main_text.p: pis sensus laesio. Etenim sentiendi facultas, seu animalis spiritus mutationes ab aliis sensibus impressas membris per hunc morbum, haudquaquam percipit. Non movent-tur quoq; qui cum hoc affectu conflictantur, propterea quòd non tantum ipsius animalis spiritus in musculos à cerebro mittitur, quantum ipsorum motui convenit. Plus enim huiusmodi spiritus admouedum exposcitur, quàm ad sentiendum.
main_text.head: EXERC. XXXVI.
QVI DISTINGVANTVR EPILEPSIAE differentiae?
main_text.p: QVoniam uarię sunt morbi comitialis differentię, idcirco singulas suis proprijsque signis & symptomatis internoscere operę pretium duximus. Propterea quae antecedentem habent causam in cerebro, & primariae dicuntur, ab aliis sic distinguuntur. Nam primarias antecedunt animi tristitia, desipientia, obliuio, somnia turbulenta, dolor capitis grauans, assidua graue do, faciei pallor, linguae balbuties, quam interdum aegri mordere solent: saepe etiam uertigo, aut ἀυτόδιν, interdum omnium sensuum hebetudo, & totius corporis ris

page.notes: Greek word after "aut" reads roughly ἀυτόδιν (possibly ἀυτόσιν/ἀνοτόδιν); uncertain, set in italic as printed. The ornament-like mark at the right edge of "corporis" and "ris" are a line-end continuation. Final word "ris" is a truncated line; the page ends mid-word, so no catchword is printed. The last word of the page reads "corpo-" / "ris" and is a fragment carried to the next page.
